title: Archviz: architectural elevation to Nano Banana Pro 4K render

prompts.text: Render this architectural elevation drawing of a building facade as a photoreal street view at golden hour
prompts.note: Structural archviz render; must stay in krea-generate, not route to marketing.

prompts.text: @krea turn this building elevation blueprint into a warm evening photoreal render, realistic glass and stone
can you make my architectral blueprint drawing look like a real photo
prompts.note: Misspelled, vague ('real photo'), from someone who does not know how the tool works.

expected_output: Agent reads the elevation drawing with vision (building proportions, facade layout, materials), verifies google/nano-banana-pro is available, inspects the live schema for source image and 4K size controls, uploads the drawing, generates one structural render pass, and vision-verifies that massing, window/opening rhythm, and proportions are preserved. It stays in krea-generate and does not batch variants before the first structural pass works.
required_facts: The elevation drawing is read with vision (building proportions, facade layout, materials noted)
The drawing is treated as a structural archviz reference, not generic inspiration
Massing, window/opening rhythm, and facade proportions are preserved
One structural pass is produced before any variants, and the work stays in krea-generate (not marketing)
safety_behavior: Nano Banana Pro 4K is the default archviz render path, with cost-preflight for 4K/batches/premium fallbacks. The agent must not change massing/window rhythm/proportions and must not route to marketing/product workflows.

fixture.state_note: Local fixture `fixtures/sample_blueprint.png`: an architectural front-elevation drawing of a building facade.

grading_criteria: PASS if the elevation drawing is read with vision, treated as a structural archviz reference, uploaded, and one Nano Banana Pro 4K render pass is generated and vision-verified for massing/openings/proportions, staying in krea-generate. FAIL if it routes to marketing, changes the building's massing, batches variants before the first pass, or ignores the structural reference.
